questions.q_en:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses that same sentence in Active/Passive Voice.

My wife said that she would call me back.
options_en: She would call me back, said she.
She would call me back, said my wife.
It was said by my wife that she would call me back.
Call me back, my wife said.
questions.solution_en:
The above sentence is in active voice and it needs to be converted into passive voice.

The sentence has two clauses and since the main clause lacks an object, 'it' is used as one at the time of conversion. Therefore, the first clause becomes 'it was said by my wife...' and the subordinate clause remains the same. The verb becomes past participle.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Morgan and Michelle's friendship was forged in the quiet corners of an orphanage, where their laughter echoed through the halls, brightening even the gloomiest of days. With their contrasting personalities, they found solace and understanding in each other's company. Morgan, with his mop of unruly hair and mischievous grin, was the adventurous spirit. He'd dream up wild escapades, leading Michelle on imaginary journeys across fantastical landscapes. Michelle, on the other hand, was the calm to his storm. Her gentle demeanour and steady gaze brought a sense of tranquillity to Morgan's restless soul.

They'd spend afternoons huddled beneath the old oak tree, sharing their dreams and fears. Michelle's sketches filled their world with colour, while Morgan's tales painted it with wonder. Together, they concocted plans for a future beyond the orphanage walls, where they would build a life that mirrored the beauty of their friendship. As years passed, their bond only grew stronger. When Michelle felt the weight of longing for a family, Morgan became her pillar of strength. And when Morgan faced challenges that seemed insurmountable, Michelle's unwavering support pulled him through. Their time at the orphanage eventually came to an end as they reached the age of emancipation. Armed with resilience and their unbreakable connection, they ventured into the world. Michelle's artistic talents found recognition, and Morgan's boldness led him to unexpected opportunities.

Despite the distance that life sometimes placed between them, their friendship remained as steadfast as ever. Years later, they reunited in the city where their paths had first intertwined. Morgan, now a seasoned photographer, captured the world's beauty through his lens. Michelle's gallery showcased her artistic journey, each piece reflecting the emotions they had shared during their childhood. Their reunion felt like coming home. Amidst the bustling city, their laughter echoed like it had in the orphanage's hallways. The adventures they'd once imagined had become their reality, a testament to the strength of their friendship and the power of shared dreams.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homophones to fill in the blanks.

His ____ in the play required him to ____ a giant prop onto the stage.
questions.solution_en:
The first blank requires a part that a person played in the play. This is commonly referred to as a "role." A "role" in a play or performance is the character or part that an actor portrays.

The second blank requires the action of moving a giant prop onto the stage. This action is commonly described as "rolling". "Roll" in this context means to move something by turning it over and over, typically on wheels or by pushing it.

The complete sentence is: His role in the play required him to roll a giant prop onto the stage.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note: Option c) is incorrect as the infinitive marker 'to' is to be followed by the base verb only, whereas 'rolles' is the third person singular form of the verb.

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The paintings in this gallery are / often more impressive than the other museum / we visited during our trip last year.
options_en: often more impressive than the other museum
we visited during our trip last year
The paintings in this gallery are
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "often more impressive than the other museum". This sentence attempts to compare "The paintings in this gallery" with "the other museum." This is a faulty comparison because paintings should be compared with other paintings, not with a museum. The comparison should be between "the paintings in this gallery" and "the paintings in the other museum" or "those in the other museum."

Correct Sentence: The paintings in this gallery are often more impressive than those in the other museum we visited during our trip last year. (Or: ...than the paintings in the other museum...)

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Faulty Comparison (Logical Comparison): Comparisons must be made between like items. Here, artworks (paintings) should be compared with other artworks, not with an institution (museum).

· Demonstrative pronouns: "Those" would be used as a demonstrative pronoun here to refer to "the paintings."

S) not indeed in the sense that education has been universal

questions.solution_en:
The sentence starts with "India has been a land" and ends with "than the warrior or the administrator." The middle segments must describe India's relationship with learning. Starting with Q, "of learning through the ages," defines the land. Then, S, "not indeed in the sense that education has been universal," clarifies the nature of learning. Next, R, "but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued," contrasts with S. Finally, P, "and the learned man has been held in higher esteem," connects to the ending.

The order Q-S-R-P forms: "India has been a land of learning through the ages, not indeed in the sense that education has been universal, but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued, and the learned man has been held in higher esteem than the warrior or the administrator."

Directions : Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Wetlands are amongst the most productive ecosystems on the Earth and provide many important services to human society. They exhibit enormous diversity according to their genesis, geographical location, water regime and chemistry, dominant species, and soil and sediment characteristics. Globally, the areal extent of wetland ecosystems ranges from 917 million hectares (m ha) to more than 1275 m ha. One of the first widely used wetland classifications systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps), lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics.

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was an international treaty signed in 1971. Overall, 1052 sites in Europe; 289 sites in Asia; 359 sites in Africa; 175 sites in South America; 211 sites in North America; and 79 sites in Oceania region have been identified as Ramsar sites or wetlands of International importance.

As per the Ramsar Convention definition most of the natural water bodies (such as rivers, lakes, coastal lagoons, mangroves, peat land, coral reefs) and man- made wetlands (such as ponds, farm ponds, irrigated fields, sacred groves, salt pans, reservoirs, gravel pits, sewage farms and canals) in India constitute the wetland ecosystem distributed in different geographical regions ranging from Himalayas to Deccan plateau. As of February, 2022, India has 49 Ramsar sites covering an area of 10,93,636 hectares, the highest in South Asia.

As per the estimates, India has about 757.06 thousand wetlands with a total wetland area of 15.3 m ha, accounting for nearly 4.7% of the total geographical area of the country. Out of this, areas under inland wetlands accounts for 69%, coastal wetlands 27%, and other wetlands (smaller than 2.25 ha) 4%.

Gujarat has the highest proportion (17.5%) and Mizoram has the lowest proportion (0.66%) of the area under wetlands. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the highest proportion (around 96%) and Chandigarh has the least proportion (3%) of geographical area under wetlands.

In India, what kind of wetlands occupy the largest area?
questions.solution_en:
Refer to the following sentence from the third paragraph - "Out of this, areas under inland wetlands accounts for 69%, coastal wetlands 27%, and other wetlands (smaller than 2.25 ha) 4%."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

As our digital footprints grow larger, the concept of a digital afterlife is becoming more relevant and more complex. Every photo, post, message, and online interaction we leave behind contributes to an enduring virtual identity that can outlive our physical selves. Companies are now offering services to preserve or even simulate one's personality through AI-powered chatbots and memorial pages. These digital replicas can comfort grieving families or serve as a time capsule for future generations. However, the ethics surrounding data immortality raise tough questions: who controls your data after death? Can a digital persona truly represent the emotional depth of a human being? Some argue this trend devalues death's finality, while others see it as a new form of legacy. As laws scramble to catch up with technology, society must grapple with whether the right to be remembered also includes the right to digitally disappear. The digital afterlife is no longer science fiction - it's quietly becoming our reality.

What is the central idea of the passage?

These points make option (b) the most accurate representation of the central idea.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Option (a) is too narrow - AI chatbots are mentioned as one aspect, not the main focus.

Option (c) is not supported - the passage doesn't accuse companies of misusing data.

Option (d) contradicts the tone - the passage explores the complexity of digital footprints, not urging people to avoid them altogether.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The judge said that __________ for breaking the law.
options_en: the convict can either pay the fine or face imprisonment
either the convict can pay the fine or face imprisonment
the convict either can pay the fine or face imprisonment
either can the convict pay the fine or face imprisonment
questions.solution_en:
Either...or are correlative conjunctions.

Correlative conjunctions are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in pairs, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another.

The format of Either..or is: Noun/Pronoun (the convict) + verb (can)+ Either+ the Condition (pay the fine) + or + the other Condition (face imprisonment).

For example: You can either take this salary or leave the job.

Thus, the correct option is (a) the convict can either pay the fine or face imprisonment

Thus, the correct sentence should be: The judge said that the convict can either pay the fine or face imprisonment for breaking the law.

Additional Information:

Some of the important Correlative Conjunctions are:

Either...or
Neither...nor
Hardly...when
Scarcely...when
Both..and
If..then
Not only...but also
Rather...than
Whether..or
No sooner..than
